minutes.headline: Select Board denied a class 2 auto dealer license after police showed the applicant's surety bond was altered.
minutes.summary: Long public comment on the school budget shortfall, an override and the municipal building project opened the meeting, along with a retired sergeant's farewell letter. The board ratified two police appointments, denied a used-car dealer license after a police presentation, and heard the new town manager's early FY2026 budget picture and a draft warrant walk-through. Budget discussion was informational; no budget figures were voted.

public_comment.stated_role: school committee chair, speaking as a citizen
public_comment.topic: Thanked the board for the budget task force, urged action on its recommendations and CPA, and called for an override on the ballot.
Thanked voters for last year's override, warned of dozens of school positions on the chopping block, and objected to weighing a new town hall alongside school cuts.
Cited a school shortfall and urged all departments to collaborate and prioritize children.
Worried how cuts would affect her special education child, teachers and paraprofessionals.
Proposed a per-taxpayer payment instead of overrides, selling town property, and keeping town meeting doors closed during votes.
Questioned the late school budget process and the size of the stated deficit, and urged action on the town buildings.
During the license hearing, asked the board to consider whether the applicant had separated himself from the former owners and to give leeway.
Said state legislators are not representing the town and the state should be the target for more funding.
Agreed on reducing reliance on the state and repeated his per-taxpayer payment idea.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 0 to 4 against a class 2 auto dealer license at 40 Summer Street, after a police presentation on the applicant's paperwork.
The board ratified two police appointments, including one promotion to Sergeant, by unanimous vote.
The town manager gave an early FY2026 revenue picture: health insurance and county retirement increases together exceed the town's share of new revenue.
The board held the ARPA press release for a week and deferred the budget task force recommendations to next week with the full board.
Public comment on the school budget shortfall, a possible override and the town hall project ran through the first part of the meeting; nothing was decided.

why_it_matters: The town side of the FY2026 budget has limited room: preliminary health insurance and retirement increases together exceed its share of new revenue, which bears on the tax bill and on whether an override question reaches the ballot.
The task force recommendations on audit and the Community Preservation Act were deferred, so no action on them has yet been taken in response to the school budget concerns raised in public comment.
watch_next: The task force recommendations and the workplace climate survey policy return to the full board next week.
The warrant closes March 17; the town manager will present revenue and capital, not a full budget, to the finance committee on Thursday.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on every recorded vote, including the 0-4 denial of the auto dealer license, and mostly on the budget figures. They differ on two decisions: our minutes say the Budget Task Force item was deferred and that the chair would drop the internal warrant deadline, while the official minutes record a discussion and only a possible revisit.
